Detect a within-case nesting variable by name pattern then structure

Source: R/utils-formulas.R
find_nest_var.Rd

Detect a within-case nesting variable by name pattern then structure

Usage

find_nest_var(
  data,
  exclude = character(0),
  case_var = NULL,
  time_var = find_time_var(data)
)

Arguments

data

Data frame.

exclude

Character vector of column names to skip (e.g., case, study, phase, time, outcome, piecewise terms).

case_var

Optional case-grouping column. When supplied, a candidate must vary within at least one case; a column constant within every case is a between-case covariate and is rejected.

time_var

Time column used by the structural fallback; defaults to find_time_var(data).

Value

Column name (length-1 character), or NULL if no candidate is found.

Details

A column whose name matches a nest pattern (behavior, setting, target, skill, ...) qualifies when it varies within a case. Any other non-numeric column, or integer-coded column when a case column is known, with 2-20 levels (criterion, trials, IOA, and coded piecewise columns excluded) qualifies only when it splits concurrent series (time points repeat within a case but not within a case-by-column cell) or when phase onsets differ across its levels within a case, so a date or note column never becomes a nest. Without a time column the structural fallback is skipped.

Examples

d <- data.frame(
  case = rep("Ian", 8),
  behavior = rep(c("greet", "share"), 4),
  outcome = rnorm(8)
)
find_nest_var(d, exclude = "case")
#> [1] "behavior"
